origin.trigger: MT-019 full PostgreSQL proof suites passed but their process-exit test cleanup timed out after 60 seconds and left 27 exact knowledge_test schemas; 13 still existed when independently reread and required exact manual cleanup.
origin.why_a_new_mt: The defect is owned by tests/knowledge_pg_support.rs and directly belongs to MT-019 test-resource lifecycle, not MT-020 production_factory.rs. The operator requires an unexpected same-WP gap to be retained as a future MT when it does not directly belong to the current MT.

scope.summary: Make PostgreSQL integration-test schema teardown bounded, exact, and reliably leak-free for the WP-1 process-ledger and real-process lifecycle suites.
scope.root_cause: The process-exit cleanup sends many sequential DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE operations through one psql process under one aggregate 60-second budget. Full MT-019 runs exceeded that shared budget after 10 and 17 schemas, so successful tests could leave large migrated schemas behind.
forbidden_paths: Production PostgreSQL storage or migration behavior
Broad database, schema-pattern, or cluster deletion
Suppressing cleanup failures without a bounded observable receipt
Stopping PostgreSQL or any process not started by this MT
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Cleanup operates only on the exact task-owned schema names returned by the test schema allocator; no wildcard, database-wide, or cluster-wide deletion is permitted.
AC-2: Every allocated schema receives an independent bounded cleanup opportunity, so one slow DROP cannot consume the cleanup budget for later schemas.
AC-3: Best-effort process-exit cleanup remains non-panicking and observable, while normal per-test cleanup happens early enough that process exit is only a recovery fence.

AC-4: Fresh full runs of process_ledger_reclaim_tests and process_reclaim_real_lifecycle_pg_tests pass against Handshake-managed PostgreSQL and an independent canonical pg_namespace reread proves zero schemas allocated by those runs remain.
AC-5: Failure-path tests prove an individual cleanup timeout/error does not prevent later exact schemas from receiving cleanup attempts and does not target foreign schemas.
proof_commands: Independent psql query of pg_namespace for the exact schema names allocated by both proof runs; expected count: 0
scope.risk_if_missed: Repeated full PostgreSQL validation leaks hundreds of migrated objects per schema, bloats the managed catalog and disk, slows later tests, and can make otherwise-correct work appear flaky or blocked.

implementation_notes: Preserve the existing real PostgreSQL authority and exact-schema allocator.
Prefer normal-scope RAII or explicit teardown; retain process-exit cleanup only as a bounded recovery fence.
Direct every Cargo target to Handshake_Artifacts and clean it after proof.
red_team: A single larger timeout preserves the aggregate-budget bug and will regress as migrations grow; the budget must be per exact schema or cleanup must occur earlier.
Dropping every knowledge_test_* schema could delete a parallel agent's live schema; exact allocator-owned names and foreign-schema survival are mandatory.
A green test binary does not prove cleanup; pg_namespace must be reread independently after process exit.

lifecycle.proof_status: PENDING_IMPLEMENTATION: exact leak reproduced after successful MT-019 full suites; independent cleanup recovered the dedicated proof database to zero matching schemas.
lifecycle.last_runtime_status_ref: DISCOVERED_AFTER_MT019_FULL_SUITES_2026-08-14; 27 captured leaks, 13 independently present, exact cleanup completed, canonical count zero
